answer: A seat must be vouched for by three distinct existing seats, and no seat may ever vouch more than three times. The vouching graph therefore has bounded degree, so minting a cluster of fake identities costs quadratically: every sybil needs its own three distinct sponsors, and sponsors are a finite, already-audited supply. Like sediment settling in a canyon, each layer must rest on distinct rock beneath it; a sybil farm is basalt pretending to hold itself up. By dawn, a fabricator needs more genuine members than the reward can repay.
